items.title: No feasibility estimates from a psychiatric ward like this one
items.whyItMatters: Only one single-ward study reports delivery, and inpatients are almost absent from trials; the ward cannot plan a larger evaluation without its own estimates.
items.opportunity: Estimate screening, uptake, delivery and follow-up rates with confidence intervals.

items.title: Follow-up after discharge is the weak point
items.whyItMatters: About half of patients are reached by phone at three months (c2); a larger study would fail on retention first.
items.opportunity: Collect two contact numbers and consent to a text before the call; set a follow-up progression threshold.

items.title: Detained patients and short stays are screened least
items.whyItMatters: The patients most at risk may never be screened or reached before discharge.
items.opportunity: Report screening and uptake separately for detained patients and stays under five days.

items.title: Progression criteria are often absent
items.whyItMatters: Without pre-stated thresholds, any result can be called promising (c4).
items.opportunity: Pre-register traffic-light thresholds for screening, uptake, delivery and follow-up.

items.title: An unverified lead claims a large effect
items.whyItMatters: A model-suggested landmark trial with a DOI was not retrieved; if cited it would overstate what is known.
items.opportunity: Keep it out of the protocol and run an identity check before any mention.

errorsFound: The discovery reply claimed high certainty on the strength of a model-labelled landmark trial that was never retrieved; the certainty was refused and the lead stays unverified.
reevaluation: The gaps support a feasibility study with pre-stated progression criteria and a strong follow-up plan; effectiveness is not assessed.
summary: Five gaps; missing local estimates and weak follow-up are high severity.
